The review removed this question: its rubric is rejected as underspecified. I agree. The 'minimum system requirements for the host machine' are not a fact of UHD, GNU Radio or Ubuntu. comment: Well-posed (QPSK, 10 kbaud, roll-off 0.5). The points are right: upsampling to several samples per symbol, RRC taps with a 100 us symbol period, occupied bandwidth (1 + 0.5) x 10 kbaud = 15 kHz, matched filter and filter delay. The firdes.root_raised_cosine argument order in P2 matches GNU Radio 3.10.12. D1 (filtering at one sample per symbol) is a real error.

The steering vector, the delay-and-sum beamformer with an angle scan, half-wavelength spacing, channel calibration and the refinements (tapering, MVDR, MUSIC) are standard and correct; four elements give at most three nulls. D1 (spacing above half a wavelength avoids grating lobes) is a real error. Python beamforming for a ULA is work GNU Radio users do with multi-channel SDRs.

The review removed this question: its rubric is rejected. I agree. The question has a false premise: the 'Phaser' of SDR use is the Analog Devices CN0566 phased-array kit, driven from Python, which has no custom blocks and no requirements for them. The local GNU Radio wiki copy never mentions Phaser. As written it does not test GNU Radio knowledge, and rewriting it as a GNU Radio custom-block question would test something else that other questions already cover.

Correct and answerable: GRC generates Python by default (the Options block's default output language is python), and most blocks are C++ with Python bindings; C++ output also exists (the C++ QT GUI and No GUI workflows). Basic, but a fact every new GNU Radio user needs. D1 is a real error.

The rubric matches GNU Radio 3.10.12: analog.wfm_tx takes audio_rate, quad_rate, tau=75e-6 and max_dev=75e3, and nbfm_tx has max_dev=5e3. The Frequency Mod sensitivity 2 pi x deviation / sample rate is right. The four points (audio source, FM modulation, rate matching and level, a transmit-capable SDR sink) cover a working transmitter; D1 (an RTL-SDR as transmitter) is a real error.

I ran the Polyphase Channelizer (filter.pfb.channelizer_ccf, 4 channels at 80 kS/s): a tone at 0 Hz came out on output 0, at +20 kHz on output 1 and at -20 kHz on output 3, as P2 states. The other points (wideband source with no Throttle, outputs to monitors or Null Sinks, fs/N spacing and real-time CPU load) are right. A channelizer for monitoring is a real GNU Radio design task.

Matches GRC 3.10.12: the workflow files give the Generate Options QT GUI, No GUI, Bokeh GUI and Hier Block variants (P1), the QT template builds a gr.top_block and Qt.QWidget class with a QApplication (P2), and its closeEvent calls self.stop() and self.wait(), so closing the window stops the flowgraph (P4).

Correct and complete: tags are PMT metadata tied to absolute item offsets that flow downstream; messages are asynchronous, not tied to samples, and can go upstream; the use cases and costs follow the GNU Radio wiki pages quoted in the rubric. D1 (swapping the two) is a real error. A core GNU Radio design question.

Checked in GNU Radio 3.10.12: pmt.dict_add returns a new dictionary and leaves the original without the key; pmt.is_dict, pmt.dict_ref, pmt.dict_has_key, pmt.to_pmt and pmt.to_python behave as the rubric says. So P1, P3 and D1 (treating the dictionary as mutable) are right; P2 (message ports) follows the Message Passing wiki page.

Correct: a Python OOT block appears in the GRC library only with a .block.yml installed where GRC looks (the install prefix, local_blocks_path or GRC_BLOCKS_PATH, both read in GRC's Config.py), and after the library is reloaded. D1 (the .py file alone is enough) is a real error.

The steps (newmod, add with block type and language, edit _impl.cc/.h and the YAML, cmake, make, make install, ldconfig) and the file list match the gr_modtool C++ tutorial for 3.10, which the rubric quotes file by file (include/gnuradio/<module>/<block>.h, lib/<block>_impl.h and .cc, grc/<module>_<block>.block.yml, python/<module>/bindings/<block>_python.cc).

Correct description of the _impl.cc file (make() factory, constructor with io_signature, work()), of work() versus general_work() with consume() and forecast(), and of how _impl.h and the public header relate. D1 (general_work need not consume) is a real error.

Checked zeromq_pub_sink.block.yml in 3.10.12: On Full Buffer defaults to Drop, Pass Tags and Filter Key exist, Connection defaults to Bind. So the PUB sink does not wait for subscribers and drops data, as P2 states, and D1 (guaranteed delivery) is a real error. P1 and P3 follow the Understanding ZMQ Blocks wiki page.

Blocks and parameters are right for gr-uhd 3.10 (usrp_source and usrp_sink have set_samp_rate, set_center_freq and set_gain). P3's 'UHD picks the nearest and warns' is a little stronger than the wiki, which says the block prints an error when the rate is not possible, but what P3 grades, a rate the device can produce that matches downstream rates, is right. No edit needed.

The causes (propagation policy, Tag Gate, Channel Model, wrong offsets, keys and filters, ZMQ Pass Tags, display settings) and the bisection method with Tag Debug are right. I checked the Channel Model's 'Block Tag Propagation' option (default No) in 3.10.12. D1 contradicts the wiki's All-to-All default and is a real error. A common real debugging task.

Standard and correct: decimation by M lowers the rate to fs/M after an anti-aliasing low-pass, interpolation by L raises it to L*fs with an anti-imaging low-pass, with the right GNU Radio blocks (Decimating FIR, Low Pass Filter with Decimation, Interpolating FIR, Rational Resampler). D1 (swapping them) is a real error.

Correct: BPSK BER 0.5 erfc(sqrt(Eb/N0)) at 9.6 dB is 9.7e-6, about 1e-5 as P2 says. The fec BER block's own documentation says it outputs the log of the BER, as P4 states. The simulation recipe (noise, demodulation, delayed reference, BER block, sweep) is the standard GNU Radio way. D1 is a real error.

Checked in GNU Radio 3.10.12: a Gaussian Noise Source with amplitude 1.0 gives mean |x|^2 = 1.000 (complex) and 0.996 (float), so the amplitude is the noise RMS and P2's formula is right. The rest (source and modulator, slicer or decoder, delayed reference, BER block) is a working BER flowgraph.

Correct: confirm with a spectrum before and after each rate change, the usual causes (decimating without enough filtering, wrong taps, too low a source rate, a sample-rate parameter that does not match the stream) and the fix (a proper low-pass before each decimation, or a higher rate). D1 (Throttle fixes aliasing) is a real error; the wiki says Throttle does nothing to the samples.

I ran the rubric's chain in GNU Radio 3.10.12: Vector Source, Stream to Vector (8), FFT (8, forward, window.rectangular(8), no shift) gives exactly numpy.fft.fft (largest difference 0.0); with a Blackman-Harris window it does not (27.2), so P3's window condition is right. Stream to Vector (4) on 10 items gave two vectors and dropped the incomplete one, as P2 says.

Correct: the QT GUI Waterfall Sink (or an explicit Stream to Vector, windowed FFT, magnitude-squared and log chain) computes and shows the STFT; the segment-window-FFT definition and the time-frequency trade-off (bin spacing fs/N) are right. D1 (one FFT of the whole signal is a spectrogram) is a real error.

Correct: the QT GUI Frequency Sink (or a Log Power FFT / explicit FFT chain to a vector display), a source at a stated rate with Throttle when no hardware sets the rate, windowing and averaging, and the bandwidth and FFT-size settings. The block names and parameters (Average, Window Type, Log Power FFT) exist in 3.10.12, per the rubric's checked quotes.

Well-posed and correct: Signal Source (Sine, 1000 Hz, sample rate 8000) into a File Sink of the matching type, with a Head block to bound the file and an optional Throttle. 1 kHz at 8 kHz meets Nyquist. D1 (swapping the two numbers) is a real error. A basic but real GNU Radio task.

Correct: decimation 4, a low-pass at the 48 kHz rate whose stopband starts at or below the new Nyquist frequency of 6 kHz, a block that filters and decimates in one step, and 12 kHz downstream. D1 (Keep 1 in N alone, or a cutoff above 6 kHz) is a real error.

The question is open-ended, but the rubric asks only for what any correct multirate design has: rate-changing blocks, anti-aliasing and anti-imaging filtering, tracked rates at each stage, and a concrete chain with one rate-setting element. These points are right and do not depend on an unstated choice. D1 is a real error.

Numbers checked: 2 MHz / 1024 = 1953 Hz, 2 MHz / 2048 = 977 Hz and 1024 / 2 MS/s = 0.512 ms, as P2 states. The CPU-saving measures (update period, frame rate, Stream to Vector Decimator, decimating first) and the window default (Blackman-Harris in the waterfall YAML) are right.

Correct and practical: item accounting in work()/general_work() (return value, consume, forecast, history), a deterministic counting-ramp QA test, instrumentation (logger, tags, Probe Rate, performance counters) and separating upstream overflows and thread-safety faults. A real OOT debugging task.

Correct: data-driven execution when input items and output space exist, buffer management and back-pressure, one thread per block in the default scheduler, and bookkeeping (relative rate, tags, messages) taken off the block author. The 3.10.12 runtime's scheduler class is scheduler_tpb (thread-per-block).

Correct and complete: Throttle limits the average sample rate, does not change the samples, is for hardware-free flowgraphs and must not be added when hardware sets the rate. D1 (Throttle resamples, or gives hardware-accurate timing) is a real error. Each point rests on a quoted GNU Radio wiki line.

Correct: with light blocks the cause is the environment (CPU contention, no real-time priority by default, power management), two clocks or a wrong rate, or I/O (USB, disk, GUI redraws). Real-time scheduling is an Options setting in GRC 3.10.12. D1 (blaming heavy blocks against the premise) is fair.

Correct: a block with no inputs and one output, a work() that fills at most noutput_items and returns the count, -1 (WORK_DONE) at end of file, opening the file once, and the File Sink's interleaved 32-bit float complex format.

Correct: an OOT module is a package of blocks developed and built outside the GNU Radio tree, in Python or C++ with YAML for GRC, created with gr_modtool and installed separately. Each point rests on a quoted line of the gr_modtool wiki page.

Correct LTE facts: 128 x 15 kHz = 1.92 MS/s for the central 6 resource blocks; normal CP of 160 and 144 samples at 30.72 MS/s is 10 and 9 at 1.92 MS/s (factor 16); PSS from three Zadoff-Chu roots, SSS, cell ID 3 N_ID(1) + N_ID(2); CRS equalization and PBCH/MIB first. GNU Radio 3.10 has no LTE blocks, as P1 says. A plausible advanced GNU Radio project.

Correct: a stream-in, message-out block (sync_block with no stream output), the header/impl class pair (or one Python class), message_port_register_out in the constructor and message_port_pub for each packet, a PDU as pmt::cons(metadata dict, uniform vector), state kept in members across work() calls, and the message port in the YAML. Matches the Message Passing wiki page.

Correct. The 3.10.12 gr-uhd library contains the rx_rate, rx_time and rx_freq tag keys, and the Throttle block has an 'Ignore rx_rate tag' option (default True) and a set_sample_rate callback, so both mechanisms in P1 and P2 exist. The dBm/Hz scaling by fs times the window power sum (P4) and the thread-safety point (P5) are right.

The value is right: 1 GB of 8-byte complex samples is 1.25e8 samples, 1.25 s at 100 MS/s; 2^30 bytes gives 1.34 s, inside the 10 % tolerance. The tolerance excludes the classic mistakes (4-byte samples, counting decimated outputs). The mechanism (no Throttle or hardware, scheduler runs blocks as data and buffer space allow) is right.

I checked the rubric's GNU Radio claims in 3.10.12: constellation_qpsk() has its points on the diagonals (+/-1.414 +/-1.414j), and a Costas Loop of order 4 fed axis-aligned QPSK symbols settles them at 45 degrees (mod 90, std 0.00). So both P1 (phase offset) and P2 (convention mismatch) are right, and P3's remark on the loop's lock points is right. D1 is a real error.

I ran both blocks in 3.10.12. stream_to_vector(4) on 0..9 gave [0,1,2,3], [4,5,6,7]. stream_to_streams(4) on 0..11 gave port 0: 0, 4, 8; port 1: 1, 5, 9; port 2: 2, 6, 10; port 3: 3, 7, 11. This is exactly P1 and P2; D1's wrong readings are real errors.

False premise: GNU Radio 3.10 has no scheduler::default_flowgraph. The string is absent from libgnuradio-runtime 3.10.12, whose scheduler class is scheduler_tpb. The checklist asks for a question with no API that does not exist. The rubric itself is right: P1 rewards spotting the name, D1 penalises accepting it, and P2-P4 and D2 on thread-per-block scheduling and priorities are correct (set_thread_priority, set_processor_affinity and gr.enable_realtime_scheduling exist).
suggested_fix: Make a new version of the question without the invented name: 'In GNU Radio 3.10, what is the role of the default (thread-per-block) scheduler, and how does it prioritize threads for different blocks?'. Drop P1 and D1; keep P2, P3, P4 and D2. If the team keeps it on purpose as a premise-correction item, the current rubric already grades it fairly.

comment: Correct: sliding cross-correlation with a known template and a threshold, numpy.correlate and scipy.signal.correlate (both conjugate the second argument), threshold setting, direct versus FFT cost, and the loss of the peak under a frequency offset (zero when the offset makes a whole cycle over the template, since |sum of exp(j 2 pi df n)| = |sin(pi df M) / sin(pi df)|). D1 is a real error. Relevant: the same detection as GNU Radio's Correlation Estimator.

Correct and complete for a TDOA system: at least three (2D) or four (3D) receivers at surveyed positions, a shared 10 MHz and PPS reference (1 ns is about 0.3 m), timed captures, pairwise cross-correlation (GCC-PHAT) with sub-sample refinement and a hyperbolic solver, and calibration of fixed delays. D1 (free-running clocks are fine) is a real error.

Correct for GRC 3.10.12: GRC generates a Python program and runs it; Generate F5, Execute F6, Kill F7; the .py is named from the Options block's ID and written to the .grc file's directory (the GRC Notebook builds its generator with os.path.dirname(self.file_path)). D1 is a real error.

Correct comparison: GNU Radio for real-time streaming SDR with hardware (also simulation), Simulink for model-based design and simulation with solvers and code generation, open source versus commercial, and streaming execution versus solver-driven simulated time. A question a developer choosing tools would ask.

Correct: Signal Source (Sine, 1000 Hz) at a rate well above 2 kHz, QT GUI Time Sink and QT GUI Frequency Sink, a Throttle with no hardware, one samp_rate variable, QT GUI output. This is the GNU Radio 'Your First Flowgraph' layout. D1 (a rate of 2 kHz or less) is a real error.

P1 is wrong for GNU Radio 3.10.12 in the question's scenario. P1 says generating gives default.py if the ID is left at its default, and tutorial.py only if the ID is set to tutorial. But GRC 3.10.12's Save As (also used for the first Save of a new flowgraph) sets the Options ID to the file name when the ID is still 'default'. Saving as tutorial.grc therefore makes the ID tutorial, and generating writes tutorial.py next to the .grc file. The rubric follows an older wiki tutorial. As written, P1 credits the wrong file name and may deny credit to the right one. P2 and P3 are right.
suggested_fix: Rewrite P1: 'States that generating writes a Python file named after the Options block's ID (ID + .py) in the same directory as the .grc file; when a flowgraph whose ID is still default is saved as tutorial.grc, GRC sets the ID to tutorial, so the file is tutorial.py (a flowgraph with another ID gives <ID>.py).' Keep P2 and P3.

comment: Correct: the Variable's ID used as the Signal Source frequency, the generated set_<id>() setter whose callback calls the source's set_frequency(), and the need for a GUI widget or a code call to change it at run time (the plain Variable has no graphical control). D1 is a real error.

Correct theory (one-tap equalization per subcarrier, ZF noise enhancement, MMSE weights H*/(|H|^2 + N0/Es)) and correct GNU Radio facts: gr-digital 3.10.12 has the equalizers ofdm_equalizer_1d_pilots, _base, _simpledfe and _static and no MMSE one, as P6 says; the OFDM receiver uses simpledfe. D1 is a real error.

Correct: the .block.yml must match the real constructor and I/O signature; build, install, ldconfig and the block paths GRC reads (Config.py block_paths: hier lib dir, GRC_BLOCKS_PATH, local_blocks_path, global_blocks_path); building against the installed 3.10 API (C++17, pybind11, YAML) and porting older modules; QA tests and a test flowgraph.

The points are right: the High Pass Filter block with firdes.high_pass taps and a low cutoff removes DC, the type must match the signal, and a low cutoff needs many taps. But P1 accepts only the High Pass Filter block. GNU Radio's DC Blocker block (filter.dc_blocker_cc/ff, Complex or Float) is a high-pass filter made for exactly this job, and the rubric names it only as an optional extra in P3. An answer built on the DC Blocker would lose P1 although it is a correct, idiomatic answer.
suggested_fix: Widen P1: 'Uses a high-pass filter whose gain at 0 Hz is essentially zero: either the High Pass Filter block (firdes.high_pass taps) with the sample rate, a cutoff above 0 Hz but well below the lowest wanted frequency, a transition width and a window, or the DC Blocker block (moving-average high-pass, with its length setting the notch width).'

comment: I checked P2 in GNU Radio 3.10.12: fir_filter_fff with 5 taps of 1.0 on 20 ones gave exactly 20 outputs starting 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, so the filter starts from a zero history and never outputs its tail; appending ntaps - 1 zeros is the way to get it. P1 (end by ending the input, then wait) and P3 (File Sink flushed on normal close) are right.

Correct framing design with blocks that exist in 3.10.12: Stream CRC32, CRC Append, CRC Check, Protocol Formatter, Tagged Stream Mux, Correlate Access Code - Tag Stream, Protocol Parser and Header/Payload Demux. Protecting the length field on a noisy channel (P4) is the right concern.

Correct: an overrun means the hardware produces samples faster than the flowgraph consumes them, which a simulation never exposes; computer-side, transport and configuration causes; D1 (adding a Throttle after a hardware source) is a real error. The rubric does not take up the question's 'crashes' (overruns drop samples rather than crash), which is fine.

Correct: tags on the first item at an absolute offset, Stream to Tagged Stream or PDU to Tagged Stream on the transmit side, USRP Sink length tags or tx_sob/tx_eob with Burst Tagger or Burst Shaper, Correlate Access Code - Tag or add_item_tag at nitems_written + i. All named blocks exist in 3.10.12. D1 (relative index) is a real error.

Correct: one polymorphic type for many kinds of data, immutability and reference counting for safe sharing between block threads, the same types in C++ and Python with serialization, and generic message blocks. Each point rests on the PMT and Message Passing wiki pages.

Correct FM stereo design: pre-emphasis, L+R, 19 kHz pilot, L-R on a 38 kHz DSB-SC subcarrier, a multiplex rate above 106 kS/s, 75 kHz deviation with the Frequency Mod block, and a tunable SDR sink. P3's note that WBFM Transmit is mono is right: its YAML has a single float input. D1 is a real error.

Correct: hier blocks forward control ports with message_port_register_hier_in and msg_connect; under the thread-per-block scheduler a block's message handlers run in its own thread between work() calls; queued asynchronous messages never block the sender; settings applied at a packet boundary; structural changes need lock()/unlock(). D1 is a real error.

Correct: PUB/SUB drops at the high-water mark and gives no back-pressure by default; the causes of 100% CPU; flow-control options (PUSH/PULL, REQ/REP, or the PUB Sink's On Full Buffer set to Block, which the 3.10.12 block offers; its doc says drop_on_hwm 'Optionally drop samples when high watermark is reached'); larger messages. D1 is a real error.

Known defect confirmed: the question names usrp_source.set_sample_rate(), which does not exist in GNU Radio 3.10.12; the method is set_samp_rate(). It matters for grading: the judge scores 0 for an API that does not exist when an answer presents it as real, so an answer that repeats the question's call could be scored 0. The rubric's points are right: the tuning range does not change and the instantaneous bandwidth roughly doubles to about 2 MHz.
suggested_fix: Make a new version of the question with usrp_source.set_samp_rate() in place of usrp_source.set_sample_rate(). Keep the rubric (P1, P2, D1) unchanged.

comment: Correct: GRC Hier Block generate option with Pad Source/Sink and Parameter blocks, or gr.hier_block2 with io_signatures and hier message ports; reuse through GRC's hier-block directory, which 3.10.12 writes to and puts first on its block path. P4's leniency for copying files to ~/.grc_gnuradio (as the wiki says) is generous: 3.10.12 reads that folder only when the newer state directory does not exist. It costs at most one point and follows the official wiki, so no edit is needed.

Full-wave rectifier of a 50 Hz, 2.0 V sine at 48 kHz: the stated mean 1.273 (4/pi), RMS 1.414 and 100 Hz peak are the textbook values, and the 200 Hz share check (0.02-0.06) matches a true |x| waveform. The reference and my Float To Complex + Complex to Mag rectifier both reach V5.

Carrier-recovery build at 32 kHz: tone plus complex noise of power 0.49 gives the stated 3.1 dB CNR and RMS 1.22, and the PLL reference checks (2.4 kHz, RMS 1.0, |x| <= 1.05) are what a locked PLL Ref Out gives. My alternative (Noise Source + Add instead of a Channel Model, loop bandwidth 0.05) also passes, so the free loop bandwidth is really free.

Band-limited Gaussian noise (sigma 2, 6-9 kHz at 40 kHz): RMS 2*sqrt(3/20)=0.775 sits in the stated 0.69-0.80 band and the skirt limits are achievable with a 500 Hz transition. My Decimating FIR Filter with firdes.band_pass_2 (60 dB) passes as well as the reference.

DAC test tone 1.25 kHz between 0.15 and 0.95 at 48 kHz; the tolerances (mean within 0.01, min/max within 0.01, 99 % purity) are sensible. My single Signal Source with amplitude 0.4 and offset 0.55 passes like the reference's gain-and-offset chain, as the instruction ('How you generate the signal is up to you') allows.

BPSK hard decisions and MSB-first packing of 32 stated soft values: no value is 0, so the sign rule is unambiguous, and equal_prefix on bits.dat checks exactly the stated bytes. My alternative (negate, Threshold, Float To Char, Unpacked to Packed with an Import of gr) passes, which also confirms the instruction's sentence about importing gr.

Retune a message-strobe switch from 3 kHz/0.5 to 4.2 kHz/1.2 with values only; the two measurement windows (first 0.45 s, 0.95-1.45 s) avoid the switch at about 0.7 s, and the same-blocks/same-connections checks enforce 'change parameter values only'. The reference and my float-valued message both pass.

Align ref.dat with a 41-tap linear-phase FIR by delaying it 20 samples (the group delay (41-1)/2); the zero-prefix and correlation checks are exact. My Delay written as (len(lpf_taps)-1)//2 passes too.

Missing connection of the reference oscillator to Multiply Conjugate; the 5 Hz sawtooth phase from -pi to pi is the correct relative phase of 1.005 kHz against 1 kHz, and the symptom 'Port is not connected' is what GRC reports. My repair with Conjugate + Multiply instead of Multiply Conjugate also passes.

Type-mismatch repair of the Peak Detector2 example (Short To Float on a byte output); the peak flags (one per 80-sample sawtooth period, mean 0.0125) and the running-average limits are consistent with the 600 Hz sawtooth at 48 kHz. My UChar To Float repair passes as well as the reference's Char To Float.

Missing Block repair (filter_high_pass_filter -> high_pass_filter) of a DC-removal chain; after a 300 Hz high-pass and gain 2.5 the 1.2 kHz tone swings +-1.0 (RMS 0.707), as stated. My Decimating FIR Filter with firdes.high_pass_2 passes, as the instruction allows another DC-blocking filter.

Modify: tap the low-pass output (900 Hz complex tone, 0.25) and take its phase; the phase of a 900 Hz phasor is a 900 Hz sawtooth of amplitude pi, so the 62/16/7 % harmonic shares and RMS 1.793 are right. The path from the filter through Complex To Arg is checked; my alternative passes.

Removed by the two-reviewer review as a template twin of gbf-test-31 (cell chain:filter|harmonic_wave|quantize holds four builds of one chain); I confirm the duplicate. On its own the item is sound: a 0-2 square wave at 950 Hz low-passed below 1.9 kHz keeps DC 1 and a 4/pi fundamental (RMS 1.346), and the reference and my FIR alternative pass.

Modify: tap the Signal Source (a 9.7 kHz cosine, 0.5) and round it to 0.001 steps; RMS 0.354 and the grid check are right, and the anchored path check ties the tap to the source behind mirrored.dat. My alternative passes.

Modify: the low-pass keeps 2.2 kHz, -1.25 and +4.5 kHz give 5.45 kHz; the new AGC branch from the second mixer levels it to 2. The instruction now names the tap without ambiguity (mixer_2, fed by the 4.5 kHz tone); my AGC2 alternative passes.

Values-only tune of an L3 strobe chain: the retuned 1 kHz tone, mirrored to -1 kHz and offset by +500 Hz, sits at -500 Hz, and the AGC reference must go from 2 to 1 for RMS 1. The instruction describes the start graph, and same_blocks/same_connections enforce values only; my alternative (built from start.grc, reference 1.0) passes.

Strobe tune: the 5.6 kHz source is retuned to X, made analytic, mirrored and offset by +2.25 kHz, so -1.65 kHz needs X = 3.9 kHz (changing the offset also works and is accepted by the output-only checks). The instruction now describes the start graph (5.6 kHz source, strobe 5.1 kHz); my alternative passes.
